mainEntity.name: What is negative space in photography?

acceptedAnswer.text: Negative space is the quieter area around or between elements that attract attention. It can be sky, water, shadow or a relatively plain surface. Its relationship with other elements can express scale, distance, stillness or tension.

mainEntity.name: How much negative space should a photograph have?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no required percentage. Compare spacious and tighter framings and identify what the space contributes. Keep the amount that supports the feeling or relationship you want the photograph to express.

mainEntity.name: Does negative space have to be empty or white?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It may contain colour, texture or subtle detail. The term describes its relatively quiet role within the image, rather than a requirement for blank white surroundings.

mainEntity.name: Can negative space be the subject of a photograph?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A gap, an expanse or a relationship between forms may be the main reason for making the photograph. Space can carry meaning instead of merely supporting a separate object.

mainEntity.name: Does negative space always create calm?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It may suggest peace, isolation, exposure, uncertainty or another response. Subject matter, light and context influence the effect. Judge the actual image rather than assigning a fixed emotion to a spacious frame.

mainEntity.name: How do I create negative space?

acceptedAnswer.text: Explore viewpoint, distance and framing to find quieter areas around or between forms. Shadow or selective focus may also reduce detail when useful. Compare what each change adds or removes from the photograph.

Cropping can change the proportion and shape of space already recorded. It cannot add anything beyond the original frame, and it may remove space that carries meaning. Compare the crop with the full photograph before deciding.

mainEntity.name: How is negative space connected to restraint?

acceptedAnswer.text: Restraint asks what can be left out. With negative space, that also means recognising which quiet areas deserve to remain. Remove elements when their absence helps, while retaining context or complexity that matters.
